title: PR #47050 added the project-scoped rule snooze (mute) endpoint, which loads the issue/metric alert rule by id alone without scoping it to the project in the URL, so a user can mute alert rules in other organizations.

findings.explanation: The code does not construct or execute any SQL queries. All database operations use Django ORM methods (Rule.objects.get, AlertRule.objects.get, RuleSnooze.objects.get_or_create) which use parameterized queries by default. The rule_id parameter is passed as an integer ID lookup, not raw SQL.

The endpoint retrieves a rule by rule_id from the URL parameter without verifying the rule belongs to the specified project. The ProjectAlertRulePermission class permission check is applied, but the actual rule lookup at line 77-87 does not filter by the project parameter, allowing potential access to rules from other projects if an attacker guesses their IDs. The can_edit_alert_rule function checks organizational membership and team ownership but does not verify the rule belongs to the current project.
findings.suggested_fix: Filter the Rule.objects.get() and AlertRule.objects.get() queries to include project_id=project.id or verify the fetched rule belongs to the current project before proceeding with authorization checks.
